question: In a mechanically ventilated adult patient, tidal volume should be calculated using Ideal Body Weight (IBW) rather than actual body weight to avoid ventilator-induced lung injury.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Tidal volume MUST be set based on IBW (calculated from height and sex). Obese patients have normal-sized lungs for their height. Using actual body weight leads to dangerously high tidal volumes and ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Lung size correlates with height (and therefore IBW), not actual body weight. Using actual body weight in an obese patient would set excessively large tidal volumes, causing volutrauma and barotrauma. The ARDSNet lung-protective strategy specifies 6 mL/kg IBW.
